pr_title: Switch to use AzureFile management SDK
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
The old data plane SDK in AzureFileClient will be not supported. So switch to use AzureFile management SDK. Then the bug "Azure Files PV AuthorizationFailure" will be fixed.
Ref: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/azurefile-csi-driver/issues/188

/cc @andyzhangx

This is a breaking change. There will be some effects on deleting and resizing the pv which was created by the old version `kubernetes.io/azure-file`. 

If the pv is in the same resource group with the cluster, there is no more action for you to do.

If the pv is in the different resource group with the cluster, please use `kubectl annotate pv <your-pv> kubernetes.io/azure-file-resource-group=<resource-group-of-your-pv>` to add the resource group annotation. Then you can continue to use `kubernetes.io/azure-file` to manage this pv.

issue_context.title: Azure Files PV AuthorizationFailure when using advanced networking
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
currently this create file share action is also considered as data-path operation that's the reason why it failed since create file share action happens on master node which is not in selected network, in the future, this action will not be handled as data-path operation. 

as confirmed by azure file team, api-version `2019-06-01` supports this functionality, need to upgrade the api-version:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4c50ee993c82c6852eb3b3aa8dfa8ecc4bcfe330/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/azure/azure_storage.go#L24

**Why is this needed**:

/area provider/azure

review_comments: the default resource group is in `azureCloudProvider`, so it's not necessary to return `resourceGroup` here.

Acctually, `azureCloudProvider` is an interface. We can not directly get the `resourceGroup`. Need to make a type assertion and judge the result firstly. Only in the function which has handled like this can we get `resourceGroup`. Otherwise, out of the function, need to assert type again. 

So in order to reduce the duplicated code, I put the `resourceGroup` into return values.

this is restricting to use node resource group, while storage account could also be in external resource group, .e.g.
```
---
kind: StorageClass
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: azurefile
provisioner: kubernetes.io/azure-file
parameters:
  skuName: Standard_LRS
  resourceGroup: EXISTING_RESOURCE_GROUP_NAME
```
and in this PR, `f.resourceGroup` could only have one determined value, which means azure file share can only exists in node resource group, this issue could be the blocker here.

one workaround is add a new field(`azurestorageresourcegroupname`) in secret:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0c3c2cd6ac8c9ffefc38f9746034e546331b9cd6/pkg/volume/azure_file/azure_util.go#L62-L67
should make sure it's backward-compatible
I use another workaround. Set the resourceGroup into PV annotation. This way won't make users change the usage. PTAL.

https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/create-share
```
The Create Share operation creates a new share under the specified account. If the share with the same name already exists, the operation fails.
```

I think if it return error, check error message, keep same behavior as old code.
It is by design. The management plane API silent ignores the error and takes it as an update operation.
make the logic consistent with the original. See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/91723
